_meanings:
<ab>N.</ab> of the daughter
 of Viśvāmitra by the nymph Menakā who was sent down by Indra to disturb
 the sageʼs austerities. [When Menakā went up to the heaven she left the
 child in a solitary forest where she was taken care of by ‘Śakuntas’
 or birds, whence she was called “Śakuntalā”. She was afterwards found
 by the sage Kaṇva and brought up as his own daughter. When Duṣyanta
 in the course of his hunting came to the sageʼs hermitage, he was fascinated
 by her charms and prevailed on her to become his wife by the Gandharva
 form of marriage; (see Duṣyanta). She bore to him a son named Bharata,
 who became a universal monarch, and gave his name to India which came
 to be called Bharatavarṣa.]
